title: Automated QA Suite — Plant Nursery Web App
description: BDD-based QA automation framework covering the Sales and Plant modules of a group web project. Authored Gherkin feature files for API and UI test scenarios including functional flows, role-based authorization, and negative/edge cases.
features: Gherkin feature files for Sales and Plant module workflows
API test scenarios validating create, read, and delete operations
Negative test cases for unauthorized and bad-request (4xx) responses
Role-based authorization testing (admin vs. standard user flows)
Serenity BDD reports with step-level traceability
Maven build integration for repeatable test execution
testingApproach: Wrote BDD feature files in Gherkin covering happy-path and negative scenarios
Used REST Assured for HTTP-level API assertions (status codes, response bodies, headers)
Tested role-based access control — verified unauthorized endpoints correctly return 401/403
Validated CRUD operations on Sales and Plant entities end-to-end
Generated Serenity HTML reports for each test run for traceability
architecture: BDD automation framework built with Cucumber + Serenity BDD running on JUnit via Maven. REST Assured handles HTTP requests; Gherkin feature files drive test scenarios; Serenity produces living documentation reports.
challenges: Designing reusable step definitions that could handle both positive and negative API scenarios without duplication
Ensuring test isolation so each scenario starts from a known state
solutions: Introduced a shared request context object passed between Cucumber steps to eliminate parameter duplication
Used dedicated setup/teardown hooks in Cucumber to seed and clean test data before/after each scenario
lessonsLearned: BDD's Gherkin layer makes test intent readable to non-engineers, improving collaboration with developers
Negative test cases often surface more bugs than happy-path tests — investing time there pays off
Serenity's living documentation significantly reduces the manual effort of test reporting

title: CloudMart — Cloud-Native E-Commerce Platform on AWS
description: Production-grade microservices e-commerce platform deployed on AWS EKS across a custom multi-AZ VPC. Responsibilities covered network design, infrastructure-as-code with Terraform, Architecture Decision Records, disaster recovery strategy, and FinOps analysis.
features: Five containerized microservices across a custom multi-AZ VPC
Terraform IaC for reproducible infrastructure provisioning
Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) documenting key design choices
Disaster-recovery strategy with defined RTO and RPO targets
Cost and FinOps analysis for the AWS deployment
IAM roles and policies following least-privilege principle
testingApproach: Infrastructure validation — verified Terraform plans before apply and reviewed state files post-deployment
Network connectivity tests across VPC subnets and availability zones
IAM policy auditing to ensure least-privilege access per service
Disaster recovery drills — simulated AZ failure and measured recovery against defined RTO
architecture: Five Docker-containerized services orchestrated on AWS EKS within a custom multi-AZ VPC. Terraform manages all AWS resources. Traffic routed via Application Load Balancer; services communicate via internal VPC DNS.
challenges: Designing VPC CIDR blocks and subnet routing to support multi-AZ failover without IP conflicts
Keeping Terraform state consistent across team members working on the same infrastructure
solutions: Used a carefully planned CIDR allocation scheme with non-overlapping /24 subnets per AZ
Stored Terraform state in an S3 backend with DynamoDB state locking to prevent concurrent modifications
lessonsLearned: Infrastructure-as-code pays dividends immediately — rebuilding the environment for testing took minutes, not hours
Defining RTO/RPO targets before implementation forces concrete decisions about replication and failover that would otherwise be deferred
FinOps analysis during design (not after) prevents cost surprises in production

title: Tool Time Management System — Gislaved Gummi Lanka
description: Centralized web platform for the mold-making unit at Gislaved Gummi Lanka (Pvt) Ltd with role-based access for managers, machine operators, and admins. Replaced Excel-based tracking with real-time operational insights and structured reporting.
features: Role-based access control for managers, machine operators, and admins
Mold detail tracking replacing manual Excel sheets
Structured reporting and real-time operational dashboard
Data entry forms with validation for mold lifecycle events
Audit trail for all data modifications
testingApproach: Manual functional testing of all role-based access flows (admin vs. operator vs. manager views)
Form validation testing — boundary values and invalid input scenarios
End-to-end workflow testing: create mold entry → update → generate report
Cross-browser compatibility checks on Chrome and Edge
architecture: React + Material UI frontend, Spring Boot REST API backend, MongoDB document store. Role-based authorization enforced at the API layer via JWT tokens.
challenges: Translating informal Excel-based workflows into structured data models that operational staff could adopt quickly
solutions: Conducted requirement gathering sessions with operators to map existing workflows, then designed forms that mirrored familiar column structures from the Excel sheets
lessonsLearned: End-user involvement during requirements gathering is critical for enterprise tools — the initial data model assumptions were wrong and had to be revised after the first demo

title: Interns Management System (IMS)
description: Group project building a profile management and evaluation platform for university interns. Handled profile management, CV uploads, task tracking, intern evaluations, and role-based permissions. Led the team as Team Leader.
features: Intern profile management with CV upload capability
Task assignment and progress tracking per intern
Evaluation forms and scoring for intern performance reviews
Role-based permissions (intern, mentor, admin)
Reporting dashboard for program coordinators
testingApproach: Manual testing of all CRUD operations on intern profiles and task records
Role-based access testing — verified each role saw only permitted UI sections
File upload testing for CV attachments (valid formats, size limits, invalid file types)
Integration testing of evaluation form submissions and score aggregation
architecture: MERN stack: React + MUI frontend, Node.js/Express REST API, MongoDB document store. Built under supervision of 99x.
challenges: Coordinating feature development across a group of five developers on overlapping modules
Designing an evaluation scoring model flexible enough for different internship programs
solutions: Adopted a feature-branch Git workflow with pull request reviews to keep main stable
Used a configurable scoring rubric stored in MongoDB so coordinators could adjust weights without code changes
lessonsLearned: Team leadership means unblocking others first — context-switching to review PRs and resolve merge conflicts quickly was more valuable than writing features
Clear API contracts between frontend and backend teams prevent last-minute integration pain

title: Biodegradable Plate-Making Machine from Food Waste
description: Level 1 hardware project — an Arduino Mega-controlled machine converting food waste into biodegradable plates through automated blending, compression, and heating stages. Addressed environmental sustainability through accessible manufacturing.
features: Automated blending unit for food waste processing
Compression stage with pressure control
Heating element with temperature regulation
Arduino Mega microcontroller orchestrating all stages
Circuit simulation in Proteus 8.0 before physical build
testingApproach: Circuit simulation in Proteus 8.0 to validate logic before physical assembly
Unit testing each hardware stage independently (blender, compression, heater) before full integration
Temperature and timing calibration runs with measurement logging
N/A for software-based automated testing — hardware system tested through physical operation
architecture: Arduino Mega as the central controller managing three sequential hardware stages via relay modules and sensor feedback loops. Circuit designed in EasyEDA, simulated in Proteus.
challenges: Achieving consistent compression force without over-engineering the mechanical component
Managing heat distribution evenly across the plate mold
solutions: Iterative physical prototyping with measurement at each compression cycle to find the optimal dwell time
Added a thermocouple feedback loop to the Arduino to maintain target temperature within a tolerance band
lessonsLearned: Simulating circuits before physical build saved significant time and material — bugs found in Proteus cost nothing to fix
Hardware testing requires a different mindset: you cannot mock a relay — you must instrument and measure the real system
